title: Why Theo Missed $114K of Free Money 😬
description:
Nora and Theo both save $300 a month from the same $60K salary. Nora's goes into her 401(k), where her boss adds 50 cents for every dollar. Theo keeps his in his own account to stay flexible. After 25 years at 7%, Theo has about $228,000 and Nora about $342,000: a $114,000 gap that came from the match, not from saving harder.

Takeaway: an employer match is part of your pay. Find out if your plan has one and what it takes to get all of it.

Does your employer match, and are you getting the full amount? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration only: $60,000 salary each, both save 6% ($3,600/yr); match of 50% on the first 6% of pay ($1,800/yr), fully vested; same 7% average yearly return for both, contributions at year end, 25 years; before taxes and fees. Real returns vary and are not guaranteed. Match formulas and vesting rules differ by employer, and 401(k) money generally can't be withdrawn before 59½ without taxes and penalties. This is not financial advice.
